segments: Chronography of Bar Hebraeus.

he said:
"I do not doubt that he performed these things by divine power."
And he asked
whether anyone at all of his disciples remained.
And it was told him
that some remained in Jerusalem.
And he arose to go to Jerusalem.
And when he reached Sicily,
he died there, eighty-eight years old.
And in the beginning, Galen was taught by a certain physician, Aelianus,
who, when a pestilence befell the Antiochians, took theriac, went there, and gave it to them to drink.
And those who drank after they had become sick,
some of them indeed were saved,
and some of them perished.
And those who drank before the illness,
all of them were delivered.
And Claudius Ptolemy has many books on the art of astronomy.
And those which are most renowned are:
the Great Book of the Syntaxis [the Almagest],
and the Book of Geography,
and the Book of the Fruit [the Karpos / Centiloquium],
and the Four-part Book [the Tetrabiblos] on astrology.
And he was the first to make a plane [projection of] the bronze sphere that represents the heavens.
And at this time also lived Alexander of Aphrodisias,
who commented on the books of Aristotle with commentaries that were very famous among the Greeks,
and also now among the Syrians and the Saracens [Arabs].
And many examinations, disputations, and investigations were conducted between him and Galen.
And he named Galen 'mule-head',
because of the obstinacy of his head at the time of examination and debate.
For Theon the geometer, the Alexandrian, also lived at this time.
For he has books which became famous in almost the entire earth:
the Book of the Construction of Bronze Rings,
with which observations of the motions of the stars are carried out;
and the Book of the Canon,
in which he sets forth an explanation {apodosis} of the calculation of the shift of the solstitial points {tropics} towards those which follow, every eighty years one degree up to eight parts,
and they turn back again;
something which does not seem right to Ptolemy,
because apart from this addition, the calculations agree with the observations made by means of the instruments for observations. And he also has the Book of the Astrolabe,
and the Book of the Isagoge, that is, the Introduction to the Syntaxis of Ptolemy. [Page] 54
